title: Pipeline hygiene
description: A worked example on the most representative generative template. All copy below is newly written for this example — none of it is taken from the measured source site.

content.title: Keep every pipeline record worth trusting
content.sub: Close the gaps in your records before a rep ever sees them, so nobody works a stale account.

content.heading: Hygiene that runs on its own
content.body: Records drift the moment they land. Watch for the drift, repair it in place, and let the team keep working.

cards.title: Spot the gaps early
cards.body: Flag records that are missing the fields your routing rules actually depend on.

cards.title: Repair in place
cards.body: Fill the gap from the sources you already pay for, without exporting a thing.

cards.title: Keep the fix durable
cards.body: Re-check on a schedule so a record you repaired once stays repaired.

content.text: We stopped arguing about whose numbers were right and started working the same list.

rows.title: See what is missing before anyone works it
rows.body: Score every record against the fields your motion needs, then sort the queue by what is actually fixable today.

rows.title: Repair from the sources you already pay for
rows.body: Run a waterfall over the gaps and write the result straight back to the record, with the provider that answered attached.

rows.title: Re-check on a schedule, not on a hunch
rows.body: Set how often a record should be revisited and let the repair run quietly in the background.
